## TL;DR

Built the Hub from this task worktree with Xcode and exercised its sidebar, add/edit/remove flows, Settings, Cmd-K switcher, loopback health state, and quit/relaunch persistence. The review found and fixed one small UI defect: once a server had a repository name, its sidebar subtitle showed that name instead of the saved URL. A regression test covers the case, and the native Xcode test suite passed. I also connected the isolated Hub to the managed task preview and verified that the actual RepoOS Control UI loaded inside the embedded web view.

I used a disposable registry directory and a separate QA bundle identifier for interactive work. One initial launch did not inherit the temporary registry setting and displayed the normal saved server list; I did not select or mutate those entries, but the Hub selected its saved localhost:7171 page and local discovery displayed a `repoos` result. I stopped that process and moved subsequent runs to an isolated registry. The task preview was then started with RepoOS's preview command, added to the disposable Hub registry, and its Control screen was captured as `11-repoos-preview-in-hub.png`.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification and macOS Hub README, confirmed the host is macOS, and ran `xcodebuild` with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` and a dedicated DerivedData directory outside the repository. The build succeeded. The first normal app launch read the existing user registry because Foundation resolves the home directory from the account record rather than the shell's `HOME`. I made no saved-server changes. I added `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` as an explicit registry path override and covered it with a unit test. I also used `launchctl setenv` for the QA process so relaunches inherited the temporary path; it was unset at the end.

The first pass against the isolated QA registry added `http://127.0.0.1:17867` by URL to a loopback health endpoint named `QA Sandbox`. The Hub saved it as Healthy and loaded the endpoint in the embedded web view. Editing the row to `QA Hub Edited` and accent color `22AA66` showed that the second line changed to `QA Sandbox` instead of retaining `127.0.0.1:17867`. The intended row hierarchy is the editable server name above its connection address. I extracted the subtitle selection into a small helper that always uses the stored origin (with the scheme stripped, consistent with the existing presentation) and added a test for a server with a different repository name. The UI then showed the edited name and the URL in the sidebar in both Dark and Light system appearance.

I exercised the server context menu and editor, opened Settings, and confirmed Cmd-K listed the server, its full URL, and recent page. I stopped the test endpoint and used Reload to confirm Offline status and its action panel. After quitting and relaunching, the saved row and Offline state remained. I removed the test entry through the UI, restored Dark appearance, quit the QA Hub, stopped the fixture, and removed the temporary launch environment. No QA process or listener remained on port 17867.

The UI captures were made with `screencapture -l<windowid>` for the Hub window only. I opened and inspected each image; the desktop was never captured. They are retained outside the worktree in `/Users/nick/Library/Caches/RepoOS/task-1167-shots/`:

## Approaches tried

Shell `HOME` isolation did not change the app's Application Support location. I added a support-directory override and test, built with a separate QA bundle identifier, and used a dedicated registry outside the repository. Applying that bundle identifier to `xcodebuild test` failed `testScaffoldHasStableAppIdentity`, as expected from the repository's identity guard; rerunning tests with the normal identifier passed. I kept the unique identifier only on the interactive QA build. Each screenshot used the Hub window ID and I visually inspected all captures.

I attempted to start the worktree RepoOS server using `just serve-noauth 17867`. It started, but the runtime log reported binding to `0.0.0.0` because Tailscale was detected. I stopped it immediately. The just recipe's log says localhost, but its command does not pass `--host 127.0.0.1`. A direct retry with an explicit loopback host was refused by the managed-agent guard (`Managed agent processes may not launch repoos serve`). I switched to the server-managed task preview instead. Adding its loopback URL to the isolated Hub loaded the real RepoOS page; the embedded view showed Control, navigation, live server status, and dashboard content. I captured and inspected the app window only.

## Challenges and blockers

The interactive test process and the app's own server registry needed separate isolation. The shell's `HOME` variable was insufficient; the explicit support-directory override made the app's file writes target a disposable registry. The test entry was removed in the UI, then I deleted the disposable registry and home directories after quitting the QA app. An initial non-isolated process showed the normal saved entries and loaded its selected localhost page, although I made no edits, additions, or removals there; later sessions used the isolated registry.

The managed preview made it possible to verify real page rendering without launching an unmanaged RepoOS server or touching Nick's saved registry. The Hub showed a healthy connection and rendered the preview's live Control page. The preview and Hub were stopped after capture, and the isolated registry was removed; no app process launched for this QA remained running.

## Key learnings

A server's repository name is useful metadata, but it must not replace the saved address in a sidebar whose job is to identify both what the entry is called and where it connects. The UI regression surfaced only after editing an entry whose health response included `projectName`; the existing row test did not cover that state, so the new pure helper test makes the behavior explicit.

For Hub QA, test data isolation must be established in the app's path resolution, not inferred from shell environment conventions. Also, loopback-only development-server claims need to be checked against the actual startup binding on hosts with Tailscale; the observed recipe output and effective bind address differed. This report keeps those environmental limits separate from the Hub behavior that was actually exercised.
